label: Semolina pudding
note: Semolina cooked with milk, or milk and water; eaten in Europe since Roman times (Apicius describes a farina porridge); instant versions use milk powder

about.text: Porridge-like pudding of semolina cooked in milk, served with sugar, cinnamon, fruit or syrup.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Milk, or milk and water, or water alone
Thicker baked version with more semolina; Syrian mamonia toasts the semolina in butter first
